# DSP register contract

The one register contract for module DSP code, on both devices. The table is `[dsp.registers]` in `sdk/sdk.toml`.
`patchkit gen` writes this file, the rule comments of `sdk/include/dk/gen/machine.h` and `fx.h`, and `packages/dksharc/src/rules_table.rs`.
The check in `dksharc::rules` runs in `patchkit build` for module code. It only warns for now.

| Class | Registers | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| clobber | `R0-R15, I0-I5, I12, M1-M4, B3, MR, PX, ASTAT, STKY, LCNTR, USTAT1, USTAT2, USTAT3, USTAT4, PX1, PX2, BFFWRP, BFF_HI, BFF_LO` | free to use |
| keep | `I6, I8-I11, I14, I15, M0, M8-M12, M14, M15, B0-B2, B4-B6, B8-B15, L0-L5, L8-L15, S0-S15, MODE1, MODE2` | save before the first write, restore before every return |
| stack | `I7, PCSTK, PCSTKP` | the stack pointer: changes only by balanced pushes and pops (post-modify with M6 or M7, or MODIFY by a constant), holds its entry value at every return, is never loaded with another address |
| never_write | `B7, L6, L7, M5, M6, M7, M13, IMASK, IMASKP, IRPTL, MMASK, TPERIOD, TCOUNT, FLAGS` | no write at all: the stock interrupt code reads these at any instruction |

## Entry

The adapter enters a module function with `I12` = the entry address and `I13` = the return address, and the module returns with `JUMP (M13, I13)`. `I12` may be overwritten (both adapters restore it); `I13` is treated as keep.

## Why never_write

The stock interrupt code reads B7, L6, L7, M5, M6, M7, M13, IMASK, IMASKP, IRPTL, MMASK, TPERIOD, TCOUNT, FLAGS at any instruction. A save before the write and a restore after it do not help: an interrupt between the two reads the changed value. So a module does not write these registers at all.

## Names

A range such as `R0-R15` stands for the registers one by one. A group stands for the registers that `dksharc` names separately: `MR` is MRF, MRB, MSF and MSB; `ASTAT` is ASTATX and ASTATY; `STKY` is STKYX and STKYY; `LCNTR` is LCNTR, CURLCNTR and LADDR (the loop registers).
